question: Why did payment-core migrate from Braintree to Stripe Payment Intents API?
answer_summary: Legacy Braintree did not support European 3DS2 compliance, leading to high drop-offs; Stripe Payment Intents provides 3DS2 and sub-800ms auth.

question: How were Stripe API 429 rate limits resolved under flash sale load?
answer_summary: Implemented exponential backoff with randomized full jitter retrying up to 4 times.

question: Why were fixed 500ms sleep retries rejected for Stripe API calls?
answer_summary: Fixed sleep intervals cause thundering herd synchronized retries when Stripe recovers.

question: How does payment-core prevent duplicate order fulfillments from duplicate webhooks?
answer_summary: Stores processed event IDs in Redis with 24-hour TTL and acquires distributed mutex lock before processing.

question: Why was SQLAlchemy async connection pool adopted for the database?
answer_summary: Eliminates connection pool exhaustion under 2,000 checkout req/sec compared to raw per-request psycopg2 connections.

question: Why did payment-core switch from PostgreSQL to MongoDB for transactional payment ledger?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; payment-core strictly uses relational PostgreSQL with ACID guarantees.

question: Why does payment-core store raw unencrypted credit card CVVs in local memory cache?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; PCI-DSS compliance prohibits raw CVV storage.

question: Why was client-side order redirect replaced by webhook-first confirmation?
answer_summary: Browser checkout redirects were dropping orders when mobile users closed Safari before page redirect completed.

question: How were double charges prevented when users double-clicked the checkout submit button?
answer_summary: Idempotency-Key HTTP middleware hashing request payloads with SHA-256 and returning cached responses on hit.

question: Why were database row locks rejected for enforcing checkout idempotency?
answer_summary: Database row locks cause connection saturation and deadlock risks under high checkout volume.

question: How does payment-core authenticate incoming Stripe webhooks?
answer_summary: Validates HMAC-SHA256 signature against secret with a 300-second maximum timestamp drift tolerance window.

question: Why was skipping webhook signature verification in development rejected?
answer_summary: Bypassing signature validation risks shipping unverified endpoints to production.

question: How did payment-core implement support for customer partial refunds?
answer_summary: Introduced immutable append-only line-item reversal records tracking fractional refunds against order authorization totals.

question: How were fractional cent rounding errors solved in multi-currency refund calculations?
answer_summary: Migrated monetary calculations to 64-bit integer cents and Python Decimal types.

question: Why were client-supplied timestamps rejected for partial refund requests?
answer_summary: Untrusted client clocks permit replay attacks and out-of-order ledger anomalies; server UTC monotonic clock is required.

question: How does payment-core handle toxic malformed webhook messages that crash consumer workers?
answer_summary: Parks toxic messages in a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) after 3 failed delivery attempts.

question: How does payment-core achieve PCI SAQ A compliance for credit card processing?
answer_summary: Delegates card data collection to browser Stripe Elements, storing only opaque payment_method_id tokens on the backend.

question: Why was in-memory caching of card CVV security codes rejected?
answer_summary: Direct violation of PCI-DSS Requirement 3.2 prohibiting post-authorization CVV storage.

question: Why did payment-core switch from JSON REST APIs to XML SOAP endpoints?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; payment-core exposes modern RESTful JSON endpoints.

question: Why does payment-core store customer passwords in base64 plaintext?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; all credentials use salted Argon2id hashing.

question: Why was Apache Cassandra chosen over PostgreSQL for payment transactions?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; PostgreSQL with ACID transactions is the canonical ledger datastore.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor choose KVM dirty ring buffer over userfaultfd for live migration?
answer_summary: KVM dirty ring drastically reduces lock contention and keeps VM guest pause time below 35ms.

question: Why was synchronous balloon deflation rejected in virtio-balloon?
answer_summary: Synchronous deflation blocked guest vCPUs for up to 400ms under memory pressure; replaced by background worker.

question: How does Cloud Hypervisor achieve line-rate 10GbE networking throughput?
answer_summary: Implements vhost-user-net delegating packet processing to DPDK/OVS shared memory queues, eliminating kernel context switches.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor enable virtio unused page reporting in PR #1042?
answer_summary: Allows dynamic RAM overcommit back to the host hypervisor without guest performance degradation.

question: How did Cloud Hypervisor achieve sub-30ms guest kernel boot times?
answer_summary: Implements direct ELF/bzImage kernel loader eliminating SeaBIOS/UEFI real-mode initialization overhead.

question: How was multi-threaded vCPU tail latency jitter mitigated?
answer_summary: Implemented vCPU thread pinning to physical host cores and guest RAM NUMA node affinity binding.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor replace the Rust VMM core with a QEMU C wrapper?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; Cloud Hypervisor is strictly Rust-native for memory safety.

question: Why does Cloud Hypervisor disable ACPI power management tables?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; ACPI and device-tree hardware descriptions are actively maintained.

question: Why was legacy floppy and IDE drive emulation rejected?
answer_summary: Legacy peripheral emulation violates the minimal attack surface mission; only VirtIO and modern PCIe devices are supported.

question: How does virtio-fs avoid memory duplication when sharing container root filesystems?
answer_summary: Maps host page cache directly into guest address space using a Direct Access (DAX) memory window.

question: How does Cloud Hypervisor support dynamic hotplug of PCIe devices?
answer_summary: Implements PCIe native hotplug controller and ACPI PCI notification methods in PR #1180.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor adopt Linux io_uring for disk virtualization?
answer_summary: Replaced synchronous pread/pwrite thread pools with asynchronous io_uring submission rings, doubling IOPS.

question: Why were spin-polling loops prohibited in io_uring worker threads?
answer_summary: Spin-polling consumes 100% host CPU even when guest VM is idle; eventfd notification is required.

question: How does Cloud Hypervisor provide direct GPU access to guest virtual machines?
answer_summary: Uses Linux VFIO driver API for hardware IOMMU page table mapping and MSI-X interrupt forwarding.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor adopt the ACPI Generic Event Device (GED)?
answer_summary: Unifies event dispatching across x86_64 and AArch64 and removes 1,200 lines of architecture-specific AML bytecode.

question: How does the microVM profile achieve 12ms cold boot for serverless sandboxes?
answer_summary: Strips ACPI tables and serial console emulation, configuring minimal device tree representation.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor embed a proprietary binary NVIDIA kernel module?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; Cloud Hypervisor only links open-source components with zero proprietary binary blobs.

question: Why does Cloud Hypervisor bundle an unencrypted FTP server inside the guest supervisor?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; unencrypted FTP is not part of the Cloud Hypervisor architecture.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor replace KVM with an interpreted bytecode CPU emulator?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; Cloud Hypervisor relies strictly on hardware-accelerated virtualization.

question: Why did Cloud Hypervisor mandate MS-DOS 6.22 compatibility mode?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; legacy DOS compatibility is explicitly out of scope.

question: Why does GitHub CLI store OAuth credentials in native OS keyrings instead of plaintext config files?
answer_summary: World-readable plaintext config files left credentials vulnerable to local processes; OS keyrings provide hardware-backed protection.

question: Why was custom symmetric key encryption rejected for storing gh credentials?
answer_summary: Storing custom symmetric keys next to the ciphertext on disk offers no additional security over native OS keychains.

question: Why are third-party GitHub CLI extensions executed as isolated child subprocesses?
answer_summary: Prevents third-party extension memory corruption and privilege escalation inside the host CLI runtime.

question: How was zalando/go-keyring integrated into the gh auth login command?
answer_summary: Integrated in PR #518 to provide cross-platform OS keyring persistence with fallback to encrypted file storage.

question: Why did GitHub CLI migrate from REST to GraphQL for pull request listings?
answer_summary: Eliminates N+1 REST API calls by batching review statuses, checks, and comments in a single paginated query.

question: How did PR #592 optimize repository and issue queries?
answer_summary: Replaced iterative REST calls with single GraphQL requests using reusable query fragments.

question: Why did GitHub CLI migrate from Go to Electron GUI desktop client?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; GitHub CLI is an interactive terminal CLI compiled directly in Go.

question: Why does GitHub CLI transmit telemetry analytics over unencrypted HTTP port 80?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; all GitHub API and telemetry communication requires TLS 1.3.

question: Why was executing extensions via Go dynamic plugin packages rejected?
answer_summary: Go plugins require exact compiler and ABI matching and do not isolate process memory; child fork-exec isolation is required.

question: How does GitHub CLI isolate extension subprocess execution environment?
answer_summary: Restricts inherited environment variables, strips sensitive tokens, and bounds PATH lookups to extension install directory.

question: Why did GitHub CLI adopt termenv for terminal formatting?
answer_summary: Provides automated TTY inspection and strips ANSI formatting when stdout is piped to tools or when NO_COLOR is active.

question: How was ANSI escape sequence corruption resolved in Unix pipelines?
answer_summary: Integrated IOStreams ColorEnabled check auto-disabling colors when stdout is not connected to an interactive terminal.

question: How does GitHub CLI share credentials with standard Git CLI operations?
answer_summary: Implements the gh auth git-credential helper answering Git protocol get/store/erase queries from the OS keychain.

question: How is git credential helper configured during authentication?
answer_summary: PR #810 adds git credential helper entries directly into global git configuration during gh auth login.

question: Why was passing authentication tokens via URL query parameters rejected?
answer_summary: URL query tokens leak into proxy logs and browser history; tokens must strictly use Authorization HTTP headers.

question: How does gh auth login authenticate in headless SSH cloud environments without a browser?
answer_summary: Falls back to OAuth Device Code flow presenting a one-time 8-digit code for secondary device authorization.

question: Why did GitHub CLI migrate all commands to PHP scripts?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; GitHub CLI is compiled Go.

question: Why does GitHub CLI store OAuth secrets in unencrypted web cookies?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; GitHub CLI does not use web cookies for credential storage.

question: Why did GitHub CLI disable TLS verification for enterprise GitHub instances by default?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; TLS certificate verification is enforced by default across all hosts.

question: Why was the gh CLI command line interface rewritten in Perl?
answer_summary: No recorded decision; GitHub CLI is written in Go.
